nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S^{-1}$ be the inverse of its frame operator. The canonical dual frame is the family $(S^{-1} f_i)_{i \in \iota}$.
nodes.title: Canonical dual frame

nodes.summary: For a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, the frame operator $S$ of the family satisfies $S x = \sum_{i \in \iota} \langle f_i, x \rangle f_i$ for every $x \in E$, where the inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument.
nodes.title: Frame operator formula

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with frame operator $S$ and inverse frame operator $S^{-1}$. Then $S \circ S^{-1}$ is the identity operator on $E$.
nodes.title: The inverse frame operator is a right inverse

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S^{-1}$ be the inverse of its frame operator. Then the frame operator of the canonical dual frame $(S^{-1} f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is $S^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Frame operator of the canonical dual frame

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ whose lower and upper frame bounds are both equal to $A$. Then its frame operator is $S = A \cdot I$, where $I$ is the identity operator on $E$.
nodes.title: Tight frames have scalar frame operator

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with frame operator $S$ and inverse frame operator $S^{-1}$. Then $S^{-1} \circ S$ is the identity operator on $E$.
nodes.title: The inverse frame operator is a left inverse

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Its frame operator $S$ is invertible in the algebra of bounded linear operators on $E$, and the inverse frame operator $S^{-1}$ is its inverse there.
nodes.title: Inverse frame operator

nodes.summary: For a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, the frame operator is the bounded linear operator $S \colon E \to E$ given by $S x = \sum_{i \in \iota} \langle f_i, x \rangle f_i$, the sum of the rank-one operators $x \mapsto \langle f_i, x \rangle f_i$. The inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument.
nodes.title: Frame operator

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$, with $\iota$ finite, be a frame with bounds $A$ and $B$ in a Hilbert space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S^{-1}$ be the inverse of its frame operator. Then every $x \in E$ satisfies $x = \sum_{i \in \iota} \langle f_i, S^{-1} x \rangle f_i$.
nodes.title: Frame reconstruction formula

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be the frame operator of a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in E$, $\langle S x, x \rangle = \sum_{i \in \iota} |\langle f_i, x \rangle|^2$; the right side is a real number, viewed as an element of $\mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the frame operator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with inner product conjugate-linear in the first argument, and let $S$ be the frame operator of a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in $E$. Then $\langle S x, y \rangle = \sum_{i \in \iota} \overline{\langle f_i, x \rangle} \, \langle f_i, y \rangle$ for all $x, y \in E$.
nodes.title: Inner product against the frame operator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$ and frame operator $S$. Then the canonical dual frame $(S^{-1} f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is a frame with lower frame bound $1/B$ and upper frame bound $1/A$.
nodes.title: The canonical dual frame is a frame

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. A finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in $E$ is a frame with frame bounds $A, B \in \mathbb{R}$ if $A > 0$, $B > 0$ and, for every $x \in E$, $A \|x\|^2 \le \sum_{i \in \iota} |\langle f_i, x \rangle|^2 \le B \|x\|^2$.
nodes.title: Finite frame

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$. Then the inverse $S^{-1}$ of its frame operator $S$ is self-adjoint.
nodes.title: The inverse frame operator is self-adjoint

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in $E$, not necessarily a frame, the frame operator of $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is self-adjoint.
nodes.title: The frame operator is self-adjoint

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$. Then its frame operator $S$ is a unit in the algebra of bounded linear operators on $E$, that is, $S$ has a bounded linear two-sided inverse.
nodes.title: The frame operator of a frame is invertible

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$ and frame operator $S$. Then $A \|x\| \le \|S x\|$ for every $x \in E$.
nodes.title: The frame operator is bounded below

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$. Then $A \|x\|^2 \le \sum_{i \in \iota} |\langle f_i, x \rangle|^2$ for every $x \in E$.
nodes.title: Lower frame inequality

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite frame in $E$ with frame bounds $A$ and $B$ and frame operator $S$. Then the operator norm of $S$ satisfies $\|S\| \le B$.
nodes.title: The frame operator has norm at most the upper frame bound

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an inner product space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in $E$ is a frame with frame bounds $A$ and $B$, then $A > 0$.
nodes.title: The lower frame bound is positive

nodes.summary: If a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$) is a frame with frame bounds $A$ and $B$, then $0 < B$.
nodes.title: The upper frame bound is positive

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite family in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), with frame operator $S$. For every $x \in E$, $\operatorname{Re} \langle S x, x \rangle = \sum_{i} |\langle f_i, x \rangle|^2$.
nodes.title: Real part of the frame quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite family in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), with frame operator $S$. For all $x, y \in E$,
nodes.title: Cauchy–Schwarz bound for the frame operator

nodes.summary: If a finite family $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ in an inner product space $E$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$) is a frame with frame bounds $A$ and $B$, then $\sum_{i} |\langle f_i, x \rangle|^2 \le B \|x\|^2$ for every $x \in E$.
nodes.title: Upper frame inequality

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
